name: gap_continuation_5s_2
author: adapted from quant_system
thesis: Large gaps (>1.5%) that DON'T fill in the first 30 minutes signal genuine information (earnings, sector news, upgrade/downgrade). These unfilled gaps tend to continue in the gap direction for the rest of the session because the information hasn't been fully priced in. The inefficiency exists because most traders either fade all gaps (Strategy 3 mindset) or wait too long to confirm continuation. Not fully arbitraged because large gaps are infrequent and require conviction to trade in the gap direction.
mechanism: Large opening gaps that hold above the prior range indicate a genuine overnight revaluation. Participants who missed the gap chase the move, while short-sellers who are wrong-footed cover into the trend. The resulting buy pressure sustains the gap direction for the first 30-60 minutes until the new equilibrium is established.

indicators.name: gap_filled_30
indicators.formula: boolean: did price touch prev_close in first 360 bars?

exit.signal_exit: exit if price re-enters first 30-min range for 5 bars

weaknesses: Very low frequency: large unfilled gaps that continue are 1-3 per week across 200 stocks. Not enough trades for a standalone strategy.
Gap continuation can fail spectacularly when the initial catalyst is overreacted to — the reversal from a failed continuation is fast and large.
Slippage on gap days is worse than normal. The 4 bps assumption may be optimistic for less liquid NIFTY 200 names.
prior_art: Gap and go / gap continuation. See: trade-ideas.com literature, Andrew Aziz 'How to Day Trade'. The unfilled gap filter is the key addition.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
